name: s96-quality-gate-sigterm-spares-caller
setup_commands: export CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR='{TMPROOT}'; printf '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' '{TMPROOT}/src/x.py' | bash '{KIT_ROOT}/.claude/hooks/quality-gate.sh' >/dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!; sleep 2; cp=$(cat .checkpid 2>/dev/null || true); if [ -z "$cp" ]; then echo 'check never started: nothing to prove' >&2; exit 1; fi; if [ "$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ | tr -d ' ')" != "$(ps -o pgid= -p $pid | tr -d ' ')" ]; then echo 'hook is not in the caller process group: this test cannot detect a group kill' >&2; exit 1; fi; kill -TERM $pid; rc=0; wait "$pid" || rc=$?; printf 'caller survived the hook TERM, hook rc=%s\n' "$rc" >> caller-alive.log; case "$rc" in 0|143) ;; *) echo "hook exited $rc, expected 0 or 143" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; sleep 1; if kill -0 "$cp" 2>/dev/null; then kill -9 "$cp" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "check still running after SIGTERM (pid $cp)" >&2; exit 1; fi
notes: TAN-6278. The gate's SIGTERM trap must end the CHECK and nothing else. The hook runs in its own caller's process group — a non-interactive shell does not give a background job a group of its own — so a trap that killed its own group (kill -- -$$, killpg(0, ...)) would take the caller with it: in a real session that is Claude Code. The setup asserts the shared group first, so the test cannot pass vacuously, then TERMs the hook and keeps running: the line it appends afterwards is what file_grew checks, and it is never written if the setup shell was signalled. run_with_timeout gives the check its own session, and the trap signals only that; s92 covers the other half, that the check does not outlive the hook.
